Application Materials.content:
- Upload clear scanned copies of your **degree certificate (if completed)** and **final or current transcript**, as well as any other supporting documents. The university states: “We will not be able to assess your application without them.”
- Do not send original copies in the post, as they will be unable to return these.
- Depending on the course, you may also need to provide **two references**, including at least one who can comment on your academic ability. References must be **dated within two years** of the date of your application and, if not submitted directly by your referee, **signed and on letter-headed paper**.
- The university may also require a **personal statement**. Applicants can refer to the university’s [guidance](https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/careers/students/furtherstudy/applying.aspx "Writing a personal statement for further study") or [contact us](https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/help-and-support/home/contact-us.html).
- Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI): AI tools may help structure materials such as personal statements or check readability, but generating all or a large part of application submissions and communications using an AI tool and presenting this as your own work or words could affect the outcome of the application.
- Admissions may, at their discretion, ask applicants to provide further information to assess the application fairly and accurately. This can include **CVs, references (academic and professional)** and clarifications regarding previous and current education.

Academic Requirements.content:
- Entry requirement: **2:1 BSc degree** in mathematics, physics, economics, computer science, natural sciences or engineering.
- Applicants need **a solid background in mathematics**, including **calculus, linear algebra and the basics of probability and statistics**.
- For EU / International students: **Equivalent of a 2:1 BSc degree of the UK standard** in mathematics, physics, economics, computer science, natural sciences or engineering, with a solid background in mathematics, including calculus, linear algebra and the basics of probability and statistics.
- Alternative qualifications: applicants are treated on an individual basis, and the University may also consider **relevant work experience**.
- China applicants: applicants should hold a **bachelors degree of a good standard from a recognised university**, usually in a relevant subject area. Entry requirements for degrees from Chinese universities vary depending on the university studied at and the course applied for.
- China applicants: for courses requiring a **2:1**, the Chinese grade equivalence varies by institution tier; the stated range for **2:1** is **72% - 80%**.
- China applicants: HND/SQA AD (**BB/BBB/60%/Merit**) + final year/top-ups to a UK Bachelor degree, and 3 years Chinese Junior Diploma (Dazhuan) + 1/2 years final years/top-ups to a Bachelor degree, may be accepted as long as applicants meet the grade requirement, such as **2:1**, in both parts of the programme.
- China applicants: Bachelor degrees obtained via **2-year China Diploma plus 1-year top-up in the UK cannot be accepted** by any Departments/Schools at UoN.
- China applicants: for a **3+1 joint programme**, the University would expect an offer to be made on the second part, but applicants must also have achieved the requirement, such as **2:1**, in part 1. For a **2+2 joint programme**, the decision will be made only based on overseas transcripts.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
- IELTS: **6.0 with no less than 5.5 in each area**.
- As well as IELTS, the University also accepts other [English language qualifications](https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/studywithus/international-applicants/english-language.aspx), including **TOEFL iBT, Pearson PTE, GCSE, IB and O level English**.
- If you need support to meet the required level, you may be able to attend a presessional English course. If you successfully complete your presessional course to the required level, you can then progress to your degree course and **won't need to retake IELTS or equivalent**.
- For on-campus presessional English courses, you must take **IELTS for UKVI** to meet visa regulations. For online presessional courses, see the CELE [webpages](https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/cele/presessional/index.aspx) for guidance.
- For applicants from China: if you successfully completed a UK Degree **within two years of University of Nottingham course start date**, where at least **one full academic year was physically taught in the UK** (including HND/SQA AD+1 and top up), then this would usually satisfy the English language requirements of your course.

Program Overview.content:
Data Analytics and AI MSc is a full-time, 12-month interdisciplinary programme starting in September 2026; part-time study is not available. It provides a solid foundation in data analytics and artificial intelligence and is taught principally by the School of Mathematical Sciences, with the option to choose modules from the Business School. The curriculum teaches how approaches in data analytics and AI can be applied to decision making in modern, data-rich environments.
In addition to the core data analytics component, the programme includes options to specialise in:
- Modelling and AI for health sciences and pharmacology
- Data-driven techniques for business analytics
- Statistical machine learning and AI
The flexible structure gives students an opportunity to specialise or keep their options open, aligning their education with career goals and interests. Students develop a strong mathematical foundation along with practical and interdisciplinary skills, learn the theory behind data analytics and AI, and practise tackling real-world challenges.
This course is ideal for:
- **Aspiring data professionals** looking to work in data analysis, data science, machine learning and AI
- **STEM graduates and professionals** wanting to improve their data skills and solve real-world problems
- **Industry professionals** aiming to learn modern data analytics, statistics and AI techniques
- **Non-STEM professionals** wishing to switch to data-driven careers
The course follows a modular structure, with students completing **180 credits** over a **12-month** period: **20 credits** of core modules and **40 credits** of optional modules in the autumn semester, **60 credits** of optional modules in the spring semester, and a **60-credit** dissertation project in the summer semester. Dissertation projects may be completed in collaboration with industry or as funded placements, co-supervised by industrial partners. Students also have opportunities for summer placements, co-supervised projects with leading industry partners, guest lectures from experts in finance, pharmaceuticals and health technology, and industry-relevant dissertation projects.
Teaching is delivered through lectures, workshops, computer labs, problem-solving classes and hands-on sessions, with practical application through individual reports, posters and projects, plus collaborative learning through group projects. Assessment includes coursework, examinations, dissertation and project work, including programming. During June, July and August, students work on the dissertation, supported by a minimum of three one-to-one supervision meetings with a supervisor.
The programme is based at University Park Campus. Students have access to libraries, shops, cafes, the Students’ Union, the sports village and a health centre; free hopper buses connect to other campuses, and Nottingham city centre is 15 minutes away by public bus or tram.
Graduates of this programme are industry-ready and can pursue careers in technology, finance, healthcare and more. With strong maths and computational skills, graduates can understand and use complex data analytics and AI methods, making them highly desirable in the job market. Graduates from the School of Mathematical Sciences go on to work for top employers such as Capital One, Kubrick Group, BAE Systems, Amazon, BP and China Zheshang Bank. **92.6%** of postgraduates from the School of Mathematical Sciences secured graduate level employment or further study within 15 months of graduation, with an average starting salary of **£30,476** (HESA Graduate Outcomes 2017/18-2022/23).
The School of Mathematical Sciences is ranked Top 100 in the world for Statistics and Operational Research in the QS World University Rankings by Subject 2025, Top 3 in the UK for quality of research environment in Mathematical Sciences in the Research Excellence Framework 2021, and **98%** of its research is classed as **‘world-leading’ or ‘internationally excellent’**.

Curriculum.content:
Data Analytics and AI MSc is offered full-time over **12 months**; part-time is **not available**. The course follows a modular structure, with students completing **180 credits** over a 12-month period:
- **20 credits** of core modules and **40 credits** of optional modules in the autumn semester
- **60 credits** of optional modules in the spring semester
- In the summer semester, students work on a **60-credit** dissertation project to develop interest and expertise in a specific topic at the frontier of data analytics and AI. There will also be opportunities to complete the dissertation project in collaboration with industry or as funded placements, co-supervised by industrial partners.
The programme includes options to specialise in:
- Modelling and AI for health sciences and pharmacology
- Data-driven techniques for business analytics
- Statistical machine learning and AI
Core modules:
- Applied Statistics and Probability
- Project in Data Analytics and AI
Optional modules (autumn):
- Foundations of Data Analytics
- Foundational Business Analytics
- Data at Scale: Management, Processing and Visualisation
- Mathematical Medicine and Biology
- Application Driven Biomedical Modelling
- Advanced Statistical Inference
- Statistical Modelling with Machine Learning
- Optimization
- Financial Mathematics
Optional modules (spring):
- Analytics Specialisations and Applications
- Machine Learning and Predictive Analytics
- Applied Multivariate Statistics
- Bayesian Data Analysis
- Neural Networks and AI
- Data Science for Structured Data
- Model-informed Pharmacology
- Biomedical Modelling in an AI World
- Computational Applied Mathematics
Teaching will be delivered through a combination of lectures, problem-solving classes and hands-on computer lab sessions. Learning methods include lectures, workshops, computer labs and group study. Modules are assessed with a mix of coursework, exams, a dissertation and project work; project work will include programming.
Students will be awarded the Master of Science degree provided they have successfully completed the taught stage by achieving a weighted average mark of at least **50%**, with no more than **40 credits below 50%** and at most **20 credits below 40%**. Students must also achieve a mark of at least **50%** in the dissertation.
The course is taught at University Park Campus. During June, July and August, students work on the dissertation, supported by a minimum of three one-to-one supervision meetings with the supervisor. The number of formal contact hours varies depending on optional modules; as a guide, in the Autumn and Spring semesters students typically spend around **14 hours per week** in lectures.

Cost of Attendance.content:
How much you spend depends on your personal situation, lifestyle, and choices. The list below details possible expenses related to studying in Nottingham. These are indicative costs, accurate as of **June 2026** but subject to change at any time.
| Expense | Cost |
| --- | --- |
| [Weekly rent in University of Nottingham accommodation portfolio (bills included)](https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/studentservices/services/accommodation.aspx) | £99.00 - £312.00 |
| Approximate weekly private rent in a Nottingham student house share | £133.00 |
| [Single bus journey (student)](https://www.nctx.co.uk/students) | £2.50; [hopper buses](https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/sustainability/transport/travellingbetweencampuses/hopper-buses.aspx) between campuses are free |
| [Single tram journey](https://www.thetram.net/tickets/one-off-tickets) (student) | £3.00 |
| [Hot lunch on campus](https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/hospitality/cafesbars/universitypark.aspx) | £2.15 - £9.50 |
| [Takeaway coffee on campus](https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/hospitality/cafesbars/cafes-and-bars.aspx) | £1.20 - £4.10 |
| [Annual TV licence](https://www.tvlicensing.co.uk/check-if-you-need-one/for-your-home/students-aud1) | £180.50 |
| [September-June gym membership on campus](https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/sport/membership/studentsportsmembership.aspx) | £289.00 or free for students living in certain Halls of Residence via the [active living package](https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/sport/membership/active-living.aspx) |
| [Access to Microsoft 365](https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/dts/knowledge-hub/microsoft-365/microsoft-365.aspx) | Free to staff and students at the University of Nottingham |
Other variable costs you may need to factor into your budget include food and groceries, mobile phone bills, travel outside of Nottingham, course costs including books, stationary and printing, toiletries, clothing and shoes, haircuts and personal care, streaming services, other subscriptions, celebration events, entertainment/socialising, car/vehicle costs, broadband packages and contents insurance. You may also have larger one-off costs at the beginning of the year such as a laptop or bike.

Financial Aid.content:
Automatic scholarships for international master's students: University of Nottingham is offering scholarships worth **£3,000** to students starting their studies in **2026**. **This will be automatically awarded and will be deducted from your master's tuition fee.** Enrol and automatically receive the £3,000 scholarship; no scholarship application needed.
Eligibility: students must be an international fee-paying student; be starting year one of a full-time postgraduate taught master's degree programme (UK campus-based); be studying towards one of the following awards: MA, **MSc**, MArch, MBA, LLM, MPA, MPH or MMedSci; and be self-funded, and not in receipt of any other University award or sponsorship by an external organisation. For a two year master's degree the scholarship only applies to the first year's fees. [See full terms and conditions](https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/studywithus/international-applicants/scholarships-funding-finance/termsconditions.aspx "International scholarship terms and conditions"). Students progressing to the University from Kaplan (University of Nottingham International College or Digital Pathways) are not eligible for this scholarship scheme; however, students may be eligible for Kaplan - University of Nottingham specific scholarships.
